notes.summary: Primary-source audit and bounded-product calculus: BEGZ Theorem 1.16 is used only for cohomologous closed positive currents with a verified small unbounded locus. Bounded nonclosed product identities and domination are derived locally, not imported as intersection invariance.
notes.detailedSummary: The independently consulted primary text is BEGZ, Acta Math. 205 (2010), printed pp. 217–218, for the precise closed singularity comparison. Demailly I.5.23–5.24 was read in a public reproduction of his book after the author-hosted PDF timed out. The note fixes actual finite-level products, proves their bounded smooth-background algebra and positivity by local regularization, and proves the bounded surface mass identity and domination needed later. No E1 assumption, nonclosed monotonicity theorem, rooftop continuity, Siu theorem, or PDE normalization is used.
notes.text:
This is an unverified mathematical draft and a source audit, not an execution certificate.

The unchanged assignment and its statement-only targets are the input, saved as input.json. I consulted only public foundational sources, not a target author's proof or another worker's material. The indispensable non-elementary closed comparison premise is BEGZ, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math. 205 (2010), Theorem 1.16, printed pp. 217–218. The complete statement and printed proof on those pages were read in the author-hosted public PDF [BEGZ](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf). Its precise hypotheses are closed positive currents, a common cohomology class for each corresponding pair, a compact Kähler manifold, small unbounded loci, and the stated ordinary singularity order. Applying it in both directions gives equality of top masses for equivalent potentials under those hypotheses. It supplies no comparison for a nonclosed background. The remaining local Bedford–Taylor continuity and non-pluripolar locality are the conventions explicitly permitted by the assignment. No energy result is needed below.

The author-hosted Demailly book link is [Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf); it timed out. The actual primary text I read was its public reproduction [Demailly I.5.23–5.24](https://www.scribd.com/document/947528850/Demailly-Complex-Differential-and-Analytic-Geometry), including the preceding proof. The allowed removable-singularity premise requires a closed pluripolar set and a psh function locally bounded above near it; its extension is unique as a genuine psh representative. The later descent proof also spells out its elementary barrier argument for an analytic center. No other primary-source theorem is indispensable.

Here are the bounded-product facts used subsequently. On a coordinate ball, take a smooth strictly psh function r with L=dd^c r dominating any of the finitely many smooth backgrounds under consideration. If v is bounded and θ+dd^c v≥0, ψ=v+r is bounded psh and A=L−θ is smooth. Define the actual bounded θ-product by the finite expansion (dd^c ψ−A)^k. This is precisely the smooth-background correction prescription. Independence of r follows by expanding after adding a smooth function to ψ; the local Bedford–Taylor algebra gives the same expressions. For smooth gauges the same observation will be used in n5.

These bounded products are positive when θ+dd^c v is positive. For completeness, convolve on a smaller coordinate ball. Then dd^c(v*χ_ε)+θ*χ_ε≥0. Since θ*χ_ε−θ tends uniformly to zero, adding e_ε dd^c|z|² with e_ε↓0 makes dd^c(v*χ_ε)+θ positive. One can convolve the psh ψ with radial approximate identities, which decrease to ψ. The smooth correction errors tend to zero. Bedford–Taylor decreasing continuity shows that the powers of these positive smooth forms converge to the displayed corrected product. This proves positivity without a nonclosed intersection theorem. The same argument proves that taking a maximum of two θ-psh functions preserves θ-psh admissibility: apply smooth convex maxima to the regularizations, retain the common lower bound −θ−o(1), and pass to the canonical limit.

On the compact Kähler surface used here, for bounded v the corrected algebra gives
 M_θ(v)=∫θ²+2∫θ∧dd^c v+∫(dd^c v)²
       =∫θ²+2∫v dd^c θ.                                      (1)
The last quadratic term integrates to zero because it is dd^c(v dd^c v), a globally defined distribution. One can define v dd^c v using a closed smooth auxiliary Kähler form as v(K+dd^c v)−vK; the local Bedford–Taylor definition gives the same differential identity. Stokes against the constant function gives zero. The middle term is integration by parts against a smooth form. Thus (1) is proved for actual bounded products and does not assert that nonclosed raw mass is invariant.

If K is closed positive, K≥θ, and both θ+dd^c v and K+dd^c v are positive, set β=K−θ. On a surface the bounded corrected algebra gives
 (K+dd^c v)²−(θ+dd^c v)²
    =2β∧(θ+dd^c v)+β²≥0.                                   (2)
Only a positive current wedged with a smooth positive form occurs on the right. This proves the domination used in n3.

For θ≥0 and any θ-psh v with sup v≤0, the genuine truncations v_j=max(v,−j) are bounded θ-psh. By non-pluripolar locality the measures
 1_{v>−j}(θ+dd^c v_j)²
are increasing and agree with the extended product on their respective level sets. Their limit is the finite-level non-pluripolar measure from the question. The discarded set is {v=−∞}. More generally a local bounded admissible barrier B−j may be used for a background which is not semipositive: max(v,B−j) is admissible and gives increasing domains exhausting the finite locus. Corrected bounded products on overlaps agree by locality. This gives positive extended Borel measures without evaluating an ∞−∞ expression. They give zero mass to pluripolar sets; this follows level by level from bounded Bedford–Taylor products and their smooth corrections. Covariance under coordinate biholomorphisms follows by smooth approximation and decreasing continuity.

notes.summary: Reference imposed type and Target E: the genuine sublogarithmic pole is nonanalytic, has zero Lelong numbers and trivial I(tu) for all t>0. Its actual closed K-product has full mass, with finite first moment exactly for α<1/2.
notes.detailedSummary: In coordinates x=|z|²/(1+|z|²), w pushes forward to dx, G_p=log x, and t=1−log x. The one-dimensional curvature measure Cw+dd^c U has density [(C−αt^(α−1))e^(1−t)+α(1−α)t^(α−2)(1−e^(1−t))]dt, no atom at p, and total mass C. Hence MA_K(u)=2C(Cw1+dd^c u)w2 has mass 2C². The first-moment tail is asymptotic to 2Cα(1−α)∫t^(2α−2)dt; at α=1/2 its divergence is (C/2)log T. This establishes full mass independently of E1, throughout 0<α<1.
notes.text:
All statements here are mathematical proofs subject to independent verification. Use the dd^c normalization in the question. By a Fubini–Study isometry take p=0 on the first P1. Put
 w=dd^c log(1+|z|²),  G_p=log(|z|²/(1+|z|²)).
Then dd^c G_p=[p]−w, max G_p=0, and the genuine value at p is −∞. Write φ(t)=1−(1−t)^α on t≤0. Its derivatives satisfy
 φ′(t)=α(1−t)^(α−1)∈(0,α],  φ″(t)=α(1−α)(1−t)^(α−2)>0.
Away from p, the actual curvature of U=φ(G_p) is
 dd^c U=−φ′(G_p)w+φ″(G_p)(i/(2π))∂G_p∧bar∂G_p.             (3)
Thus αw+dd^c U≥0 off p. Locally add α times a smooth potential of w and extend the resulting bounded-above psh function across p by the permitted canonical removable theorem. This gives the genuine quasi-psh U with U(p)=−∞ and the global inequality. A direct radial calculation below shows there is no atom at p, so (3), extended without an atom, is its complete distributional curvature.

The pole behaves as −(log(1/|z|²))^α+O(1) at p. Consequently U divided by log|z|² tends to zero, so its Lelong number is zero. The pulled-back u has zero Lelong numbers at all points of D={p}×P1, and is smooth elsewhere. It is unbounded on D. An unbounded analytic singularity β log(Σ|f_j|²)+O(1), β>0, has all its generators vanishing at a pole and hence has a positive logarithmic coefficient there. Therefore this u is not analytic, even up to ordinary equivalence. For every t0>0,
 ∫_0^ε exp(t0 O((log(1/r²))^α)) r dr <∞,
because after q=log(1/r²) the exponent is −q+O(q^α), with α<1. Holomorphic germs are bounded on a smaller neighborhood. Hence every germ is locally integrable with the exact weight |g|² exp(−t0u), and I(t0u)=O_X for every real t0>0. There is no extra factor 2 in this argument.

Here is the actual measure calculation. Let x=|z|²/(1+|z|²) and t=1−log x. The radial pushforward of probability w is dx on [0,1]. Angular integration of (i/(2π))∂G_p∧bar∂G_p gives ((1−x)/x)dx. For any C≥α, let ρ_C=Cw+dd^c U. On 0<x<1 its radial density is
 f_C(x)=C−α(1−log x)^(α−1)
        +α(1−α)(1−log x)^(α−2)(1−x)/x≥0.
The exact cumulative mass is
 ρ_C({x≤ε})=Cε+α(1−ε)(1−log ε)^(α−1).                    (4)
Indeed its derivative is f_C, and the flux at x=0 vanishes since α<1. Formula (4) tends to zero at ε=0 and equals C at ε=1. It proves both absence of a pole atom and total mass C, using genuine measures rather than formal wedge classes.

Choose C≥max(c,max a,α), so the closed Kähler form K=C(w1+w2) dominates θ. Since u depends only on the first factor, the actual bounded products away from D, and then their non-pluripolar extensions, give
 MA_K(u)=2C (Cw1+dd^c u)∧w2,
 MA_K(u)(X)=2C²=∫K².                                    (5)
To check the product passage directly, truncate U on the base. The square of the first-factor current is zero at each bounded level, by dimension one, so the product is the displayed mixed measure on each retained level set. These exhaust X\D; (4) shows that the omitted tail has mass tending to zero. Thus (5) is an actual closed non-pluripolar product and proves full mass for every α∈(0,1).

In the t coordinate the full density of ρ_C, with positive orientation toward the pole, is
 r_C(t)=[C−αt^(α−1)]e^(1−t)
          +α(1−α)t^(α−2)[1−e^(1−t)],       1≤t<∞.        (6)
Since −U=t^α−1, the first moment is exactly the nonnegative integral
 ∫_X(−u)MA_K(u)=2C∫_1^∞(t^α−1)r_C(t)dt.                 (7)
The exponentially decaying part is integrable. The remaining integrand is asymptotic to α(1−α)t^(2α−2), with a positive coefficient. Consequently (7) is finite if and only if α<1/2. At α=1/2 the integral up to t=T equals (C/2)log T+O(1); at α>1/2 its leading divergence is
 [2Cα(1−α)/(2α−1)] T^(2α−1).
This is the precise logarithmic boundary for the actual measure, not an imposed premise. In particular full mass and a finite first moment are distinct.

The reference u is θ-psh for θ=cw1+a w2, c≥α, a>0, because the first-factor current cw+dd^c U is nonnegative and the vertical coefficient a is positive. The divisor D is a closed locally complete pluripolar set, defined locally by z=0, and u is locally bounded outside D. These are the small-unbounded-locus facts required for the closed comparison in n3.

Rerun diagnostics with python check_reconstruction.py > artifacts/check_stdout.txt 2> artifacts/check_stderr.txt. The symbolic check differentiates (4) and obtains exactly f_C. The numerical first moments use (6)–(7), not a discretized formal product. Their scope is illustrative; the endpoint criterion is proved by (6)–(7).

notes.summary: Target A reconstructed for every full-variable equivalent competitor: actual extended mass is ∫θ²+2∫v dd^cθ, and the exact ordinary-type extrema are 2c min a and 2c max a. A closed full-mass domination argument handles all rough product passages without a first moment.
notes.detailedSummary: For K≥θ, equivalence to u and the verified divisor unbounded locus allow BEGZ Theorem 1.16 in both directions, giving full closed K-mass for every competitor. The discarded θ-truncation tail is bounded by the vanishing K-tail. Fiber averaging yields a positive base curvature measure ρ=cw+dd^cF of mass c, and Mθ(v)=2∫aρ. Actual equivalent separated competitors retain the reference curvature near p and move all remaining mass via smooth Green corrections. Their weak residual closure is every positive base measure of mass c. This also gives BMP and positive lower mass for the product Hermitian backgrounds, distinctly from first-moment finiteness.
notes.text:
Fix 0<α<1, c≥α, a>0 smooth on P1 and θ=cw1+a w2. This form is smooth strictly positive: θ≥min(c,min a)(w1+w2). Thus the actual representative 0 is a strict current, proving bigness in the definition of the task. Since dθ=da∧w2, it is nonclosed whenever a is nonconstant. Also dd^cθ=dd^c a∧w2; on P1 a nonconstant smooth a cannot have dd^c a=0.

Let v be an arbitrary full-variable θ-psh function ordinarily equivalent to u. There is B<∞ with u−B≤v≤u+B, including the canonical values −∞ on D. In particular v is locally bounded outside the closed locally complete pluripolar divisor D. Choose K=C(w1+w2) as in n2. Then K+dd^c v and K+dd^c u are cohomologous closed positive currents on the compact Kähler surface X. Both have small unbounded locus D. Their potentials have mutual ordinary singularity order. The permitted, primary-read closed comparison theorem, applied in both directions with two factors, therefore gives
 ∫MA_K(v)=∫MA_K(u)=∫K².                                  (8)
This use meets every listed hypothesis and is confined to the closed background K.

Normalize v by a finite constant so sup v≤0, and put v_j=max(v,−j). Each is an actual bounded θ-psh and K-psh representative. Closed bounded Stokes gives ∫MA_K(v_j)=∫K². By non-pluripolar locality and (8),
 ∫_{v≤−j} MA_K(v_j)
   =∫K²−∫_{v>−j} MA_K(v_j) →0.                           (9)
By n1's bounded domination,
 0≤∫_{v≤−j} MA_θ(v_j)≤∫_{v≤−j} MA_K(v_j)→0.             (10)
Thus the increasing retained θ-products have finite total mass equal to the limit of the complete bounded products. The bounded formula (1), and L1 convergence v_j→v against the smooth dd^cθ, yield the actual identity
 MA_θ^ext(v)(X)=∫θ²+2∫v dd^cθ.                            (11)
Every product passage has now been justified; in particular no integral (−v)MA_K(v) was assumed finite. The only potential integrability used is ordinary local L1 of quasi-psh functions.

For the unrestricted optimization, take the genuine fiber average
 F(x)=∫_{P1}v(x,y)w(y).
Outside p this is finite and satisfies U−B≤F≤U+B. At p set F(p)=−∞. Upper semicontinuity follows from reverse Fatou with a local uniform upper bound; at p the displayed bound forces the limit to −∞. Averaging after adding a smooth potential of cw on a base chart proves the genuine subharmonic representative. Equivalently, wedging the positive current θ+dd^c v with smooth w2 and pushing forward gives
 ρ=cw+dd^c F≥0,  ρ(P1)=c.                                (12)
Fiber dependence and mixed distributional derivatives cause no difficulty: pushforward commutes with dd^c and w2²=0. Distributional integration by parts against smooth a, followed by Fubini, transforms (11) into
 M_θ(v)=2c∫a w+2∫F dd^c a=2∫a dρ.                       (13)
Therefore every competitor has positive finite mass and
 2c min a≤M_θ(v)≤2c max a.                               (14)
This is the global bound for arbitrary rough full-variable competitors, not merely separated ones.

Here are actual admissible approximating representatives of the exact type. Set ρ_0=cw+dd^c U, the nonnegative atom-free measure proved in n2. Choose smooth cutoffs χ_j, equal to one on a neighborhood of p and zero outside neighborhoods shrinking to p, and set t_j=∫χ_j dρ_0→0. Given a point q realizing either min a or max a, choose a smooth nonnegative probability ν_j with support shrinking to q but avoiding p for each j. When q=p use small annuli. Define
 ρ_j=χ_jρ_0+(c−t_j)ν_j.
For large j this is a positive measure of total mass c. The signed measure ζ_j=ρ_j−ρ_0 has total mass zero and is a smooth real two-form: it vanishes near p and ρ_0 is smooth away from p. It has a smooth global Green potential h_j with dd^c h_j=ζ_j. Explicitly take
 h_j(x)=∫G_y(x)dζ_j(y),
where G_y is the Fubini–Study logarithm of squared chordal distance, dd^c_xG_y=[y]−w. The zero total mass removes the −w term. Smoothness follows locally because convolution of the logarithmic fundamental-solution distribution with a smooth compactly supported density is smooth; the remaining kernel is smooth. This proves the required solvability here without invoking an unprovided global PDE result.

Put v_j^*=pr1^*(U+h_j). Then
 θ+dd^c v_j^*=pr1^*ρ_j+a w2≥0.
The smooth h_j is bounded on compact P1, so v_j^* is ordinarily equivalent to u, canonically equal to −∞ on D. Its actual extended measure, by separated bounded products and the pole-excluding limit, is
 MA_θ^ext(v_j^*)=2a pr1^*ρ_j∧w2.
Alternatively its total mass follows from (13), already proved for all competitors. Since ρ_j converges weakly to cδ_q, its mass tends to 2ca(q). Thus
 σ_minus(θ,u)=2c min a,   σ_plus(θ,u)=2c max a.             (15)
The extrema need not be attained; actual equivalent representatives approach both. No analytic pole or loss of the prescribed sublogarithmic tail was substituted.

This gives additional residual moving data, rather than just the two endpoint numbers. Let R(θ,[u]) be the weak closure of all base measures (12) coming from full-variable equivalent representatives. It is exactly the set of all positive base measures of mass c. Indeed (12) gives one inclusion. For the other, repeat the preceding construction with smooth probabilities ν_j approximating any chosen probability, using finite atomic approximations and small smooth bumps avoiding p, and retain the same vanishing pole tail χ_jρ_0. The resulting measures converge to the prescribed c-times probability. The total-mass functional on this residual set is the continuous functional ρ↦2∫aρ; its image is the closed interval in (14). This records the vertical residual positivity a, the imposed genuine type [u], and the differential background data da and dd^c a. It is only a construction for this stated family, not a general positive-product class.

Finiteness distinctions are explicit. For the smooth positive Hermitian background h=θ itself, the same bounded formula and fiber averaging apply to every bounded h-psh function. Their masses lie in (14). Conversely smooth separated Green potentials realizing cw+dd^c F=cν_j with probabilities concentrating at either extreme approach the bounds. Hence v_−(h)=2c min a>0 and v_+(h)=2c max a<∞. Thus these backgrounds have BMP and positive lower mass, proved separately. For the closed Hermitian h0=w1+w2, bounded masses are identically ∫h0²=2 by Stokes. None of these finiteness statements imply the first moment in n2, which fails for α≥1/2. All masses here are independent of a choice of probability density m.

notes.summary: Targets B–C reconstructed over ALL smooth Gauduchon tests: V_mu=2c/H, attained by the proposed test, with exact signed subtraction derivative. The height example has a nonbig semipositive nef endpoint and logarithmic V degeneration, separate from the ordinary-type extrema.
notes.detailedSummary: For an arbitrary test with matrix entries x,y,z, fiber integration gives ∫y w2=k constant. Its denominator satisfies D²≤2AkH, where A=∫ax w1w2, while its numerator is ck+A. AM–GM proves λ≥sqrt(2c/H); the positive closed test x=cm/(Ha²), y=1, z=0 attains equality. Differentiation yields the stated minimizing-test pairing and its integral on every compact admissible segment. For a=2+τ, m=1 and η=w2, V_s=4/log((3−s)/(1−s)), σ_−=2(1−s), σ_+=2(3−s). At s=1 all-test λ=0 excludes any strict current via a pointwise matrix inequality, not by restricting a possibly singular current to a fiber.
notes.text:
This note proves B and C with the infimum taken over every smooth positive Gauduchon test. Set Ω=w1∧w2 and μ=mΩ, with m>0 smooth and ∫m w=1. Define H=∫(m/a)w. In local product unitary frames relative to w1,w2, an arbitrary positive real (1,1) test T has diagonal coefficients x,y>0 and mixed coefficient z with xy>|z|². Consequently
 θ∧T=(cy+ax)Ω,  T²=2(xy−|z|²)Ω,
 D_μ(T)=∫sqrt(2m(xy−|z|²))Ω.

The fiber integral k(x_base)=∫_{P1}y(x_base,y_fiber)w(y_fiber) is a smooth positive scalar on the first P1. Proper fiber integration commutes with dd^c. Thus dd^c T=0 implies dd^c k=0. A smooth harmonic scalar on compact connected P1 is constant, for example by integrating the squared gradient. Write this constant as k>0 and put A=∫ax Ω>0. Then the unrestricted numerator is ck+A. Dropping the nonnegative |z|² term and applying Cauchy–Schwarz to sqrt(ax) and sqrt(my/a) gives
 D_μ(T)²≤2(∫ax Ω)(∫my/a Ω)=2AkH.
Therefore
 (∫θ∧T)/D_μ(T)
 ≥(ck+A)/sqrt(2AkH)
 ≥sqrt(2c/H),                                             (16)
the last inequality being AM–GM. Mixed terms and arbitrary fiber-dependent coefficients have been included. No normalization PDE, restriction to separated tests, or claim about an extremal Gauduchon metric was assumed.

Define V=2c/H and g=Vm/(2a)=cm/(Ha). The test from the question is
 T_*=(g/a)w1+w2=[cm/(Ha²)]w1+w2.                          (17)
It is smooth strictly positive. Its first coefficient depends only on the first factor, so dT_*=0, in particular dd^c T_*=0. It has k=1, A=c, z=0. Direct integration gives
 ∫θ∧T_*=2c,  D_μ(T_*)=sqrt(2cH).
Thus (17) realizes equality in both steps of (16), proving
 λ_μ(θ)=sqrt(2c/H),  V_μ(θ)=2c/H.                         (18)
This proves actual attainment in the full test space.

Density dependence is real. If a is nonconstant, the smooth positive normalized densities m=1+ε(1/a−∫(1/a)w) for sufficiently small real ε change H by ε times the positive variance of 1/a. Hence V changes. In contrast n3's ordinary-type extrema do not involve m. Since m is a strictly positive probability and a is nonconstant,
 2c min a<V_μ(θ)<2c max a.                                (19)
There is no identification of V with either singularity volume or with a raw representative mass.

For C fix m and let c_s=c−sd≥α, a_s=a−sb>0 on a segment, with d real and b real smooth. On a compact subsegment all denominators are bounded away from zero. Let
 H_s=∫(m/a_s)w,  H_s′=∫(mb/a_s²)w,
 V_s=2c_s/H_s,  g_s=c_s m/(H_s a_s),
 T_s=[c_s m/(H_s a_s²)]w1+w2.
By the proved all-test formula, T_s is an actual minimizer at each s. Differentiating its explicit optimal value yields
 (sqrt V_s)′=−(sqrt V_s/2)(d/c_s+H_s′/H_s).               (20)
On the other hand, for η=dw1+bw2,
 ∫η∧T_s=d+(c_s/H_s)H_s′,
 D_μ(T_s)=sqrt(2c_s H_s).
Equations (20) and these actual integrals give exactly
 (sqrt V_s)′=−∫η∧T_s/D_μ(T_s).                           (21)
For any s0≤s1 in a compact admissible subsegment,
 sqrt V_{s0}−sqrt V_{s1}
   =∫_{s0}^{s1}[∫η∧T_s/D_μ(T_s)]ds.                     (22)
This is the exact signed Gauduchon subtraction cost. If η≥0 it is a nonnegative cost; no such sign is silently imposed when d,b are arbitrary. Simultaneously n3 gives σ_minus=2c_s min a_s and σ_plus=2c_s max a_s. Their possible nonsmooth dependence on s is separate from (21).

For the concrete example, probability w pushes the standard height τ to (1/2)dτ on [−1,1]. With c=1, m=1, a=2+τ and η=w2, the segment is c_s=1, a_s=2+τ−s>0 for 0≤s<1. Thus
 H_s=(1/2)log((3−s)/(1−s)),  V_s=4/log((3−s)/(1−s)),
 σ_minus=2(1−s),  σ_plus=2(3−s).                          (23)
At s=0 the raw smooth zero-potential mass is ∫θ²=4, while the three other numbers are 2, 6 and 4/log 3. The zero potential has a different ordinary type from unbounded u; its raw mass is mentioned solely for comparison.

The endpoint θ1=w1+(1+τ)w2 is smooth semipositive. It is nef in the background sense of admitting θ1+εh0≥0, with the genuine potential 0, for every ε>0 and h0=w1+w2. This statement does not invoke a closed numerical nef class. Its all-test λ is exactly zero. For the tests T_s in (17),
 0≤∫θ1∧T_s/D_μ(T_s)
   =λ_μ(θ_s)−(1−s)∫w2∧T_s/D_μ(T_s)
   ≤λ_μ(θ_s)→0.
The lower bound is semipositivity and the upper bound is subtraction of a positive term. These are admissible smooth tests for each s<1, so their quotients prove the infimum is zero.

This also proves θ1 is not big under the strict-current definition, despite allowing singular potentials. Suppose θ1+dd^c q≥εh for a genuine quasi-psh q, a smooth positive Hermitian h and ε>0. For every smooth Gauduchon T, distributional integration by parts gives
 ∫θ1∧T=∫(θ1+dd^c q)∧T≥ε∫h∧T.
The pointwise two-by-two matrix AM–GM inequality is h∧T≥sqrt(h²T²). Since μ is smooth positive,
 k_h=min_X sqrt(h²/μ)>0
and therefore ∫h∧T≥k_h D_μ(T). This would force λ_μ(θ1)≥εk_h>0, a contradiction. This argument verifies nonbigness without making an invalid restriction of q to a fiber contained in its poles.

As δ=1−s↓0, V_s is asymptotic to 4/log(2/δ), hence tends to zero logarithmically, while σ_plus tends to 4 and σ_minus tends to zero. The endpoint is outside the big positive segment. These calculations give an explicit nonclosed example with a nonanalytic imposed type and an actual variational subtraction law. They do not solve a general nef-endpoint extension or classify all lower-volume failures.

notes.detailedSummary: Local smooth-background corrections are unchanged under (θ,v)↦(θ+dd^c f,v−f). Descent is proved off the analytic center, extended with a local psh barrier, and shown positive across the center because the correction is smooth and charges it zero. Pullback admissibility follows from local convolution of the current inequality; equality on a full-measure open set gives canonical equality everywhere. Biholomorphic covariance away from the center and zero pluripolar mass prove pushforward equality, even for positive extended Borel masses. notes.text:
First consider a smooth real f on a compact complex manifold, θ′=θ+dd^c f and v′=v−f. The equality
 θ′+dd^c v′=θ+dd^c v
is an equality of actual currents, including their singularities. Canonical quasi-psh representatives remain canonical after subtracting a smooth function. Transporting u as u′=u−f gives a bijection between the corresponding ordinary-equivalent competitor sets.

For the actual product, on a coordinate chart use n1's ψ=v+r and A=dd^c r−θ. Under the gauge set r′=r+f. Then v′+r′=ψ and dd^c r′−θ′=A. At every bounded local level the corrected product (dd^c ψ−A)^n is identical. Exhaustion and locality prove equality of the non-pluripolar extended measures. If a positive extended measure has infinite total mass, this assertion uses its positive level construction, not subtraction of infinite expanded terms. Consequently both ordinary-type extrema are gauge invariant.

For a smooth Gauduchon test γ in dimension n, ∫dd^c f∧γ^(n−1)=∫f dd^c(γ^(n−1))=0. Thus the fixed-density numerator and the entire all-test quotient are unchanged; the same smooth probability μ and the same test are being used. In dimension two this is ∫dd^c f∧T=0. If f=f_s is a moving smooth gauge, its derivative contributes ∫dd^c(dot f_s)∧γ_s^(n−1)=0. In particular the subtraction pairings of n4 are preserved. Changing to the zero potential in the new background is a different current: on a surface
 ∫(θ+dd^c f)²=∫θ²+2∫f dd^cθ.
For nonconstant a, taking a sufficiently small f=εa on the first factor retains positivity and changes this raw mass since ∫a dd^c a<0. Gauge invariance here always pairs the background change with v↦v−f.

Now let π:Y→X be a proper modification between smooth connected compact complex manifolds, and let A⊂X be an analytic set off which π is a biholomorphism. Let E=π^−1(A). Both are proper closed locally complete pluripolar sets, since a local logarithm of the sum of squared analytic defining functions realizes their poles. The standard definition of modification supplies this biholomorphic complement; no factorization or resolution theorem is used.

Pullback admissibility is checked locally even for a nonclosed θ. Choose r smooth with B=dd^c r−θ≥0. For a genuine θ-psh v, ψ=v+r is psh and ψ∘π is a genuine psh function, not identically −∞ because π is generically biholomorphic and surjective. Thus v∘π is quasi-psh. To retain the exact lower bound rather than just a rough one, convolve v on a smaller chart:
 dd^c v_ε+θ_ε≥0,  θ_ε=θ*χ_ε→θ smoothly.
Pulling this smooth positive form back gives
 dd^c(v_ε∘π)+π^*θ_ε≥0.
The psh regularizations of ψ, composed with π, decrease to ψ∘π and converge locally in L1; the smooth r-convolution errors converge uniformly. Therefore v_ε∘π→v∘π in local L1. Passing to currents proves
 π^*θ+dd^c(v∘π)≥0.                                      (24)
This proves genuine canonical admissibility on exceptional fibers as well as off E.

Conversely let w be a genuine π^*θ-psh function on Y. On X\A define v=w∘π^−1. On a base coordinate ball choose the same type of r with B=dd^c r−θ≥0. Then v+r is psh off A. It is locally bounded above near A because w has a finite global upper bound on compact Y and r is smooth bounded on the chart. It therefore extends canonically to a psh ψ across A. This is exactly the permitted removable theorem. For the analytic set at issue its barrier proof can also be given directly: choose ℓ=log(Σ|g_j|²)≤0 with pole set A; for ε>0, set (v+r)+εℓ to −∞ on A. The function is upper semicontinuous and locally satisfies the psh submean criterion both off A and at its −∞ values. The usc limit as ε↓0 supplies the extension. Uniqueness follows because a genuine psh function is determined by its almost-everywhere values.

Set v=ψ−r. The exact θ-positivity holds across A. Indeed
 θ+dd^c v=dd^c ψ−B.
This current is positive off A. On A the smooth form B gives zero mass to the analytic set, while dd^c ψ is a positive matrix-valued measure. Hence no negative part is introduced on A and the full current is positive. This argument does not assume that θ has a local scalar potential. Extensions on overlapping charts agree almost everywhere and therefore canonically, giving a global θ-psh v.

Both w+r∘π and ψ∘π are genuine psh upstairs and agree on Y\E. Since E has Lebesgue measure zero, uniqueness of genuine psh representatives gives agreement everywhere. Thus w=v∘π canonically, including exceptional fiber values at poles. This proves descent and the inverse bijection
 PSH(X,θ) ↔ PSH(Y,π^*θ).
Surjectivity of π now shows ordinary inequalities correspond with the same constant in both directions; all ordinary types correspond exactly. No assumption that a singular function can be restricted to a compact fiber was needed.

For the actual product law, bounded corrected products are covariant under coordinate biholomorphisms, as justified by local approximation in n1. Their finite-level non-pluripolar exhaustions inherit this covariance on Y\E≅X\A. The upstairs measure gives E mass zero, and the downstairs measure gives A mass zero, because both are pluripolar. For every nonnegative Borel test function b,
 ∫_Y b∘π MA_{π^*θ}^ext(v∘π)
   =∫_{X\A} b MA_θ^ext(v)
   =∫_X b MA_θ^ext(v).                                   (25)
This proves π_*MA_{π^*θ}^ext(π^*v)=MA_θ^ext(v). In the finite case it is equality of finite measures. With the positive finite-level Borel extension described in n1 it also holds allowing +∞ totals; no undefined difference of infinite quantities is used. It follows immediately from the competitor bijection that the ordinary-type infimum and supremum of total mass are preserved for the PURE pullback background and type. In the present family their values remain those of n3.

Here is an explicit strict-current proof for the single point blowup of the concrete projective surface (and, by the same argument, each positive product background in this family). Write h0=w1+w2 and choose δ>0 with θ_s≥δh0 for the fixed s<1. Around the point q being blown up choose coordinates z=(z1,z2) and a smooth cutoff Q on X, equal to log(|z1|²+|z2|²) on a smaller coordinate ball and zero outside the larger ball. Q is genuine quasi-psh with value −∞ at q. Its Hessian is semipositive in the smaller punctured ball; on the compact cutoff annulus it is bounded below by −Bh0 for some finite B.

In a blowup chart π(t,ξ)=(t,tξ),
 Q∘π=log|t|²+log(1+|ξ|²)
near the exceptional divisor. The elementary one-variable normalized identity dd^c log|t|²=[t=0] gives, globally,
 π^*θ_s+ε dd^c(Q∘π)=β_s+ε[E_q],
where β_s is a smooth real form. On the exceptional divisor, π^*θ_s is strictly positive in the transverse t direction and vanishes in the ξ direction; ε dd^c log(1+|ξ|²) is strictly positive in the latter. There are no mixed terms on the divisor, so β_s is positive there and in a neighborhood. Elsewhere in the inner ball it is positive because π is a biholomorphism off the divisor and the added logarithmic Hessian is semipositive. On the cutoff annulus choose 0<ε<δ/B (with no restriction from B if B=0), giving positivity there from (δ−εB)π^*h0. Outside the cutoff support it is π^*θ_s, which is strictly positive off the divisor. Thus β_s is smooth strictly positive on compact Y and β_s≥κh_Y for some Hermitian h_Y and κ>0. We have constructed the actual genuine strict current
 π^*θ_s+dd^c[ε(Q∘π)]≥κh_Y.                               (26)
This substantiates bigness without invoking a general modification-bigness theorem. If a fixed compact subsegment is desired, use a common positive δ. Applying the same construction to the closed positive h0 gives a closed smooth strictly positive residual form β0, hence a Kähler Hermitian metric on the blowup; its bounded masses are fixed by Stokes, so BMP and positive lower mass can also be witnessed independently upstairs.

Exceptional curvature subtraction changes the background and is outside (25). No equality across such a change or documented modification jump has been asserted. For a blowup the smooth top form π^*μ vanishes along the exceptional locus and is not strictly positive. Nothing here equates fixed-density variational volumes for arbitrary smooth positive upstairs probabilities.
